newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.

text.p: $2 BLN SURPLUS IN TRADE OF GOODS AND SERVICES
Australia has reported a record $2 billion surplus in international trade in goods and services for June.
Exports rose a seasonally adjusted 20 percent above the previous month, mainly because of 1.8 billion in gold sales by the Reserve Bank.

However, economist with Deutsche-Morgan-Grenfell, Richard Yetsenga, said when the abnormal one-off sales are excluded from the past two months, exports still rose by six per cent in June. Imports of goods and services also rose by a seasonally adjusted eight per cent.
Mr Yetsenga said the current account deficit for the past financial year is likely to come in at around $17 billion which he said is the best outcome Australia has seen for a long time.

"If you compare it with the budget forecast which was done just a couple of months...Treasury forecast a deficit of $20 billion so...we've done significantly better than that for the year as a whole," he said.
MEMBERS OF AUSTRALIA'S MACCABBIAH GAMES TEAM RETURN
About 100 members of the Victorian Maccabbiah team have arrived in Melbourne to an emotional welcome.
Four team members remain hospitalised in Israel after the collapse of a bridge at the opening ceremony of the Maccabbiah games last week.
Team members told reporters they would compete at the next games in four years, despite the tragedy which claimed three Australian lives.
A funeral service will be held today for Victorian Elizabeth Sawicki who died after swallowing polluted water when the bridge collapsed.
Mrs Sawicki's brother-in law, Mark, says the family wants criminal charges laid over her death.
NSW GOVT DEFENDS ADVISER SEEKING PRE-SELECTION
The New South Wales Government says there's no reason for one of its senior advisers to stand aside while seeking Labor Party pre-selection for a seat in Federal parliament.
Carmel Niland was appointed two months ago to overhaul the administration of the juvenile justice system, and she's since announced her intention to contest the seat of Lowe, in Sydney's inner west.
Calls for Ms Niland's removal from the post have come from the opposition's spokeswoman on juvenile justice, Patricia Forsyth.
She claims Ms Nilan's political plans compromise her advisory role with the government.
But, adamant she won't budge, Ms Niland says her politics is irrelevant.
And Community Services Minister Ron Dyer has backed Ms Niland's stance rejecting the calls for her to resign.
AMERICANS ON DRUGS CHARGES IN SYDNEY
Four Americans have appeared in Sydney's Central Local Court charged with importing 20 kilograms of cocaine.
The four, a pensioner, two hairdressers and a fashion designer had been on board an Air New Zealand flight from Argentina.
Two were arrested at Sydney Airport and the other two were discoverd by Federal Police at a hotel at Parramatta, west of Sydney.
Customs officer Robert Viles said it is the biggest amount of cocaine that has ever been detected at Sydney Airport.
SPORTS STARS CALL FOR AN AUSTRALIAN REPUBLIC
Some of Australia's top sports stars have signed a declaration calling for a republic.
AFL's Ron Barassi and Justin Madden, Cricket's Zoe Goss, and Rugby Leagues' Johns brothers are just a few of the 22 sports people that support a republic.
The declaration included the lines "Ashes to Ashes Dust to Dust, the Republic is a fair dinkum must".

The crowd at the Sydney Town Hall agreed but Ron Barassi was not so sure about an his chances of being the first President because he hates beer and said you cannot have an Australian as head of state, who hates beer.
The Chairman of the Australian Republican Movement made another call for a vote on the issue.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
